headings.quote: Now it came to pass in the thirtieth year, in the fourth month, in the fifth day of the month, as I was among the captives by the river of Chebar, that the heavens were opened, and I saw visions of God. In the fifth day of the month, which was the fifth year of king Jehoiachin’s captivity, The word of the LORD came expressly unto Ezekiel the priest, the son of Buzi, in the land of the Chaldeans by the river Chebar; and the hand of the LORD was there upon him.
headings.note: Ezekiel dates by the years of “king Jehoiachin’s captivity”, not by a reigning king; Jehoiachin was then a captive. The text does not explain “the thirtieth year” of 1:1.

statements.quote: And it came to pass in the sixth year, in the sixth month, in the fifth day of the month, as I sat in mine house, and the elders of Judah sat before me, that the hand of the Lord GOD fell there upon me.
statements.why: One vision: begun at 8:1–3, it runs through 9–10 and ends at 11:24 (“So the vision that I had seen went up from me”).
statements.note: Ezekiel counts his years from “king Jehoiachin’s captivity” (1:2); this verse gives the year but names no king, so no ruler is listed.

statements.quote: And it came to pass in the twelfth year of our captivity, in the tenth month, in the fifth day of the month, that one that had escaped out of Jerusalem came unto me, saying, The city is smitten.

statements.quote: In the five and twentieth year of our captivity, in the beginning of the year, in the tenth day of the month, in the fourteenth year after that the city was smitten, in the selfsame day the hand of the LORD was upon me, and brought me thither.
statements.why: The vision of the temple begun at 40:1–4 runs to the end of the book with no new date or opening.
